verdict: Caution: lend selectively to integrated, low-leverage Coimbatore spinners with firm order books; avoid stand-alone mills with thin buffers and opaque labour.
title: Coimbatore Cotton Spinning & Yarn: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Coimbatore spinning mill buys cotton, converts it into yarn, and sells to weavers, knitters and traders; cash is made or lost on the spread between cotton cost and yarn realisation.** Cotton is the dominant input, so the import duty exemption on cotton extended to Dec 31 [3] directly changes the landed cost of the raw material and therefore the mill's margin. The business is fixed-capital and working-capital intensive, and funding requirements are typically high [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the cotton procurement strategy first; if the mill buys largely on spot without a stated hedge or inventory policy, ask how it protects the spread when cotton moves.

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in procurement and in the customer mix, not in the spindle count.** Efficient cotton procurement distinguishes the profitable mills [11], and a diversified customer base limits counterparty risk because one slow payer stretches the whole working-capital cycle [11]. Leverage and debt tenure decide who survives a downturn: low leverage keeps fixed financing costs down and longer-tenure term debt covers better [10]. So when a proposal lands, check the top-customer share and the receivables ageing; if one buyer is a large share of revenue and paying late, ask for the buyer's payment record and re-size the drawing power.

## What has changed now
**The local signal is weaker than the national one: Tamil Nadu GST collections are -3.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, 9.3 pp slower [D].** Nationally, IIP NIC 13 output is +13.1% YoY and +11.9% Apr-to-date, while bank credit is +15.2% YoY, a gap of +3.3 pp over output [D]. Peer results are mixed: Nitin Spinners reported record quarterly revenue of Rs. 875 crores, up 10.3% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 17.78% [4][6], while Sportking India's Q1FY26 revenue was Rs. 585.8 crore, down 7.6% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 12.0% [5]. Locally, bonus payment is under way in Coimbatore and Tiruppur and is likely to be over by November 5 [1][2], and Tiruppur industry leaders have spoken of a slowdown in orders [1][2]. Note the rating sources [8][9][10][11] are old methodology papers, not current issuer views.

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue integrated mills that spin and convert, because integration absorbs raw-material volatility that stand-alone yarn players cannot [7].** Avoid stand-alone spinners with high leverage and a single large buyer. Structure term debt to match the asset life, since tenure drives coverage [10], and take monthly stock-and-receivables statements, monthly sales registers, and quarterly GST returns. If monthly GST turnover falls below the prior quarter's run-rate, ask for the order book and hold fresh limits.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the local GST trend, the cotton cost after Dec 31, and bonus-related cash outflow.** If Tamil Nadu GST stays negative versus India [D], tighten. If the cotton duty exemption lapses after Dec 31 [3], re-test margins. If bonus payment slips past November 5 [1][2], ask about labour cash stress. Collect from customer: current order book, cotton inventory days, and buyer-wise receivables.
